method: Primary mass 60-75%, supporting structure 15-25%, relief 5-12%, focal accent <=5% are flexible visual guidelines. Arrange coherent weathering clusters and material logic, not uniform randomness.

medieval_timber.placement_logic: Strong timber grid, recessed pale infill, steep dark roof, 1-2 block eaves, stone damp zone below timber, asymmetrical chimney.

alpine_rustic.placement_logic: Long protective eaves, high pitched gables, snow/stone transition, substantial balconies anchored by posts.

japanese_traditional.placement_logic: Rhythmically spaced posts, deep projecting curved-look eaves, open threshold, restrained monochrome and intentional garden view.

modern_concrete.placement_logic: Use true cantilevers/recessed glass and strong proportional planes; preserve large quiet surfaces instead of ornament spam.

desert_adobe.placement_logic: Thick walls, deeply shaded niches and terraces, smaller shaded windows, low-flat roof supported by beams.

dark_fantasy.placement_logic: Readable dark silhouette needs midtone breaks; concentrate saturated accents in focal openings, not every wall block.

nature_terrain.placement_logic: Shape landforms by contour and erosion, not noise voxels. Cluster rocks/plantings according to shade, runoff, traffic and elevation.

palette_review: Can identify a coherent primary material from 30 blocks away?
Are darker/older materials placed where weather and moisture make sense?
Are trim and accents readable and rare?
Do block family, biome and story agree?
Does palette respect stair/slab directional properties?
